retail_intro: Retail's war trade finally has a round number to chase, oil within reach of three digits after Germany froze Nord Stream 2 and the first sanctions landed: a scarcity spike that, in Bloomberg's telling, the Covid crash set up [[n0082]].

retail.title: Brent Crude / BZ=F — one push from the hundred-dollar barrel
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story fits in three digits: $100 oil. The New York Times says oil prices jumped toward $100 a barrel as Ukraine developments roiled energy markets [[n1109]], and The Guardian tied the move to Russia ordering troops into Ukraine [[n1263]]. Brent closed at 96.84 USD/bbl, up 3.53% on the day and 12.25% over 20 sessions from 86.27 USD/bbl on January 24 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). For retail the war trade has a pull nothing else on the board matches: it is the one position that pays you back for the pain at the pump, a hedge against the headline and the gas bill at once. Round numbers are magnets, and $100 is the biggest magnet in commodities.
What Is Driving It

Tuesday turned threats into policy. Germany froze the Nord Stream 2 gas project as the crisis deepened, Reuters reports [[n1099]], and The Guardian links the halt to Russia's recognition of the Ukrainian republics [[n1101]]; Dutch TTF gas jumped 8.17% to 79.79 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Biden imposed new Russia sanctions, per Al Jazeera [[n1255]], and London hit Russian oligarchs and banks with targeted sanctions (GOV.UK) [[n1272]]. Reuters had already warned that commodity supplies are at risk if Russia is hit by sanctions [[n0541]], and the BBC called the crude move a surge on supply fears [[n1275]]. The spillover was broad: CBOT wheat rose 5.93% to 844.25 US cents/bu and corn 3.13%, while the S&P 500 fell 1.01% to 4,304.76 index points and the VIX climbed to 28.81 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
The Social Signal

The attention is consumer-grade, which is what makes it a retail trade. NPR ran oil surging toward $100 a barrel and what that means for you [[n1264]], the Los Angeles Times reports California gas prices moving even higher [[n1274]], and Kiplinger asked how the Russia-Ukraine conflict could affect your investments [[n1605]]: three ways of turning a geopolitical headline into a household decision. The easiest ticket is the oil ETF, and USO rose 1.24% to 65.54 USD, up 9.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). When the price at the pump and the price on the screen rise together, the trade explains itself to a first-time investor in one sentence, and that simplicity is exactly how crowded commodity trades form.
Historical Analog

Bloomberg supplies the analog: oil's spectacular Covid crash set the world up for $100 crude [[n0082]]. The mechanism is the commodity cycle in miniature: a collapse starves investment, demand returns faster than supply, and a geopolitical shock lands on a market with no slack. Retail remembers the crash end of that story; the war trade is the other end. A shorter rhyme sits inside this month. Brent is only 0.37% higher than on February 14 despite Tuesday's 3.53% jump (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), which means the mid-February premium had already leaked away once before the recognition rebuilt it. That round trip is the template for how a premium built on headlines can drain on the next calm day.
Smart Money View

Professional money is not confirming the barrel. US energy shares fell as crude rose: XLE lost 1.62%, Exxon Mobil 1.16% and Occidental Petroleum 3.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), which reads like investors pricing a spike rather than a new plateau. The supply camp is split. Middle East Eye reports Saudi Arabia rejected a US request to increase production [[n1073]] and OPEC+ says it will continue to maintain balance in oil markets [[n0122]], while the Wall Street Journal says the US nears a return to the Iran nuclear deal [[n1245]] and Reuters reports Asian refiners eager to resume Iranian oil imports as high prices bite [[n1650]]. Moscow's own market read the first round as survivable: Reuters says Sberbank and VTB shares rebounded as Russia's top banks escaped UK sanctions [[n0764]].
When the Narrative Breaks

Three observable things end the round-number story. The first is supply: a signed Iran deal [[n1245]] would add barrels to a market priced for scarcity. The second is sanctions that keep sparing the flows that matter; the Sberbank rebound [[n0764]] says the first tranche is narrower than the oil price implies, and a West that stops there leaves the premium with nothing new to feed on. The third is the tape: a Brent session that gives back Tuesday's 3.53% gain while energy stocks keep sliding would confirm the spike-not-plateau read, and a fall back toward the 86.27 USD/bbl of January 24 would erase the war premium altogether. Fund mechanics add risk for latecomers: USO's 1.24% gain against WTI's 1.41% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) is a reminder that the fund and the quoted barrel do not move one for one, and the gap can widen when the futures curve shifts.

retail.title: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — the ticket paid, then the app crashed
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The lottery ticket paid on day one. Reuters reports the Trump-linked SPAC's shares surged as Truth Social topped Apple downloads [[n0780]], and DWAC closed at 92.90 USD, up 10.18% on the session and 38.22% over 20 sessions from 67.21 USD on January 24 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), on a day the S&P 500 fell. Apptopia data cited by Reuters put App Store downloads at 170k [[n1604]], and CNBC confirmed the app topped Apple's charts [[n1611]]. Vindication against a falling market is the most addictive kind.
Where It Breaks

The product is lagging the stock. The Week reports the app crashed for 13 hours after its Monday launch [[n1609]], and Bloomberg's account of Dubsmash, no match for TikTok, dying quietly after a run at viral fame [[n1603]] is the cautionary arc for any chart-topping app. With the SPAC now priced on downloads rather than revenue, every outage is a valuation event. A session that hands back the 10.18% post-launch jump would signal that the first-day buyers have become the exit liquidity for holders who bought the rumour.

retail.title: SoFi Technologies / SOFI — a billion-dollar bet on one-stop banking
parts: Why Retail Is Here

SoFi's fans buy a vision of one financial app for everything, and now the banking software underneath it. American Banker says SoFi nabbed another tech company in its quest to be a one-stop shop [[n0769]], agreeing to buy banking software firm Technisys for $1.1B, per Banking Dive [[n0771]]. The dip-buyer pitch writes itself: SoFi closed at 10.26 USD, down 9.92% on the day and 22.86% over 20 sessions from 13.30 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), so believers see the platform getting bigger while the price gets smaller.
Where It Breaks

A 9.92% drop alongside the announcement reads like a verdict on the price, and the fintech complex offers no cover: Robinhood Markets fell 15.28% and Block 15.88% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). With the 2-year Treasury yield at 1.56%, up 57 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22), growth bought through acquisitions carries a rising cost of capital. If SoFi keeps sliding from 10.26 USD while short yields climb, the one-stop shop turns from a platform story into a value trap.

retail.title: AMC Entertainment / AMC — meme veterans count scars in a correction
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The meme army's creed is endurance, and Time just printed its slogan: 'I'm down 20 grand, but I'm still up' heads its lessons from a year of meme stock trading [[n0675]], while a WSJ+ live event revisits GameStop, Reddit and the revolution that wasn't [[n0739]]. The faithful are being tested again: AMC fell 7.99% to 16.47 USD and GameStop 2.86% to 118.06 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) on the day Reuters says the S&P 500 confirmed a correction on war fears [[n1924]].
Where It Breaks

Holding is a strategy until holding gets expensive. GameStop is still up 17.88% over 20 sessions while AMC is down 1.02% and already below its January 24 close of 16.64 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), so the two flagships no longer move as one. A correction driven by war fears drains the spare cash that meme rallies run on, and CNBC reports the Dow closed at its lowest level of 2022 so far [[n0711]]. If AMC keeps falling while GameStop holds, the coalition is splitting, and a split crowd cannot squeeze anyone.
